_note: World lines (M4b World track): furniture and props you read with A in the houses and the sanctuary, and the recurring cast (data/cast.json). Same format as dialogue.json ('lines', optional 'byLeader'); merged with it by engine/dialogue.ts. Inside jokes from bible §11, spread thin: one or two per room.

lines.text: A CRT running an emulator. The save file is called FINAL_final_v2.
Don't touch it. It's calibrated. To me.

callum.text: A CRT running an emulator. The save file is called FINAL_final_v2.
Two hundred hours in. It's a fishing game. I regret nothing.

lines.text: Comics, boxed retro games, and a binder labelled MISC (ORGANISED).
Every one of these is in a spreadsheet. I've seen the spreadsheet.

haydon.text: Comics, boxed retro games, and a binder labelled MISC (ORGANISED).
Bro has a binder for his binders.

lines.text: A greasy burger bag. The receipt: double cheeseburger, extra patty, extra cheese.
Same order since we were fourteen.
You don't change a perfect order. That's just science.

callum.text: A greasy burger bag. The receipt: double cheeseburger, extra patty, extra cheese.
The Triple Cheese. Not on the menu. On my heart.
Bro. Is a cheeseburger.

lines.text: A message on Callum's phone, face-up on the table. Sergey: "bro i am in trenches. send beat". Sent four minutes ago.
We're getting Sergey out of the trenches. Not today. But we are.
A corkboard of Patchling pins. Some of these Patchlings haven't been found yet.
Yet.
A Scottish flag tea towel. It has never dried a single dish.
It's from my gran. It's not for drying. It's for heritage.
A sampler, two monitors, and a project called "beat 47 (actually good)".
Play the one with the cowbell.
There is no cowbell.
Then it's not finished.

nolan.text: A sampler, two monitors, and a project called "beat 47 (actually good)".
Nobody press anything. That's three weeks of work. Or one good night.

lines.text: NBA 2K22. The disc hasn't left the tray in years.
They peaked. I'm not going to pretend they didn't.
Cinnamon schnapps with gold flakes in it. A sticky note: NOT FOR HEADSTANDS.
He's a different breed on the headstands.
That was one time.

nolan.text: Cinnamon schnapps with gold flakes in it. A sticky note: NOT FOR HEADSTANDS.
That note is in my mum's handwriting.

lines.text: Through the high window: the white work van, in the driveway, as always.
I know that van. That van knows me.

callum.text: Through the high window: the white work van, in the driveway, as always.
I woke up in that van once. Your dad was watching. With a coffee.
He still tells people.

lines.text: Morning, boys.
Van's still there. Just checking. Old habit.

callum.text: Callum! Sleep alright?
Not in the van this time?
...Not in the van this time.

nolan.text: Your friends are here. One of them's looking at the van again.

lines.text: A stream setup. The overlay says: BRB, TRAPPED IN VIDEO GAME.
Chat thinks it's a bit. I'm leaning into it.
A whiteboard list. Every name on it is scribbled out.
Haydon. What is this list.
Nah.

haydon.text: A whiteboard list. Every name on it is scribbled out.
We've been not seeing that for years.

lines.text: A signed poster of Haydon's favourite streamer.
I watch for research.
Four hundred hours of research.
Crisps and energy drinks. A sign on top: DO NOT TOUCH (THIS MEANS DANI).
I didn't touch. I ate.
A hammock in yellow, blue and red. Still warm.
Five more minutes, then we go.
Bro said that in 2019.
A football, scuffed from a thousand kickabouts against the wall.
This is the real football. Not the one with the hands.
A coffee pot on the stove, still warm. Colombian, obviously.
You want? Is the best coffee in the world. Is not opinion.
A tournament bracket taped up by the stove. CALLUM at the top, crossed out, DANI written over it in marker.
I won that.
The bracket says different.
Dani's shoes by the door, one lace undone. His phone charger next to them.
He's been leaving for thirty minutes.
I'm literally at the door.
Family photos: birthdays, a beach, a lot of cousins.
That's my cousin. And that one. Also that one. Is a big family, bro.
Ay, his friends! Sit, sit. You didn't eat? You didn't eat.
Dani will be ready in five minutes. Don't believe him.
I call him twelve times today. He answers once. To yell.

dani.text: Mijo. Your friends have been waiting thirty minutes.

lines.text: Rubble fills the arch. Roots grow through it; somewhere behind it, water drips.
A note taped to it, in PATCH's handwriting: ROOT HALL. RESTORE AT THE STONES. THEN I DIG. (P)
A stone door, sealed. Blue light leaks from the seam. Carved above it: TIDE GALLERY.
Something to do with Kettleport. Later.
A sealed door, deeper in. The carving's worn away. The light behind it flickers like it's thinking.
Nah. We're not opening that one today.
A teal bedroll. PATCH's label: CALLUM. DOES NOT NEED A SPREADSHEET OF HIS DREAMS.
Everyone lies down for a bit. Every team is patched up.
A grey bedroll. PATCH's label: NOLAN. WILL BE UP FIRST.
Everyone lies down for a bit. Every team is patched up.
A khaki bedroll. PATCH's label: HAYDON. SAYS HE DOESN'T SLEEP. SNORES.
Everyone lies down for a bit. Every team is patched up.
A navy bedroll. PATCH's label: DANI (LATE).
Why late? I'm here!
Dani's phone buzzes. MAMÁ (14 missed calls).
Yes Ma, I'm good, I'm with the guys, we are just—
¡MAMÁ, YA TE DIJE QUE ESTOY BIEN! ¡SÍ, COMÍ! ¡NO, NO SÉ CUÁNDO VUELVO!
...She say hi.
Everyone lies down for a bit. Every team is patched up.
PATCH's workbench: a vice, rolls of tape, and one bolt labelled IMPORTANT? (CHECK).
He's been checking for a week.
A charging cradle the size of a car. Empty: PATCH is outside, working on a fix.
He sleeps standing up in this? Respect.
A whiteboard titled FIX. 1. The world. 2. The sanctuary. 3. Callum's spreadsheet (ongoing).

callum.text: A whiteboard titled FIX. 1. The world. 2. The sanctuary. 3. Callum's spreadsheet (ongoing).
The spreadsheet is fine.

lines.text: Roots older than the hill, curled round the keepers' stones. Under the bark, something glows CRT blue.
PATCH built this world. So who planted these?
A still pool. The light under the water pulses slowly, like breathing.
Is beautiful. Don't touch it. I touched it. Is cold.
Root Hall, awake again. Took longer than my first ring.
The Hollowfolk will hear of this. Some might even come and look. Don't make it weird.
Is he famous? He look famous.
...Never mind.
It's made itself at home.
The Tally's checkpoint. The barrier is down. A sign: ROAD CLOSED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE. FURTHER NOTICE POSTPONED.
A ticket is stuck in the window: RAIN CHECK.
Who even closes a road. It's a road.
Dani's phone lights up. MAMÁ: "donde estas" "DONDE ESTAS" "contesta mijo"
I'm at a road, Ma. Is closed.
¿CÓMO QUE QUÉ ROAD? ¡UNA CARRETERA, MAMÁ! ¡CERRADA!
Tell her we said hi.
A chunk of sky, fallen and half buried. Inside, the dark is full of stars.
That's where the Orbitot come from. Bits of the skybox.
A Tally tag on a stake: SALVAGE LICENCE APPLIED FOR.
The bridge over the stream has no middle planks. A cable hangs there, sparking.
A Tally sign: BRIDGE REPAIR SCHEDULED. A ticket under it: RAIN CHECK.
Scheduled for when. The heat death of the universe?
Is okay. I jump. ...No. I don't jump.
Bro fixed a bridge with an aux cord.
It's a patch cable. Show some respect.

nolan.text: Nolan, the Tally's had this on the schedule for months. You took four minutes.
Four minutes, one cable. Put it on my resume.

lines.text: Halt. Salvage zone. Licensed staff only.
Licence office hours have been rescheduled. Indefinitely.
Fill in Form 27-B. I have never seen one finished.
So nobody is licensed. Including you.

dani.text: Halt. Salvage zone. Licensed staff only.
Hello, friend! We are only walking. Very slow.
I fill the form! ...What is a form?

lines.text: The officer is long gone, still yelling about paperwork. The stairs are clear.
Dude chased me for two minutes. Never left his clipboard.
He dropped his stash. Confiscated rain checks. From us.

haydon.text: The officer is long gone, still yelling about paperwork. The stairs are clear.
Easy. Man got out-argued by a guy in a hoodie.
He dropped the confiscated rain checks. Cardio and loot.

lines.text: KEEPERS' RELAY 1/4. SANCTUARY SIGNAL: WEAK. AWAITING REPLY.
Below it, in tiny letters: FONT: DRAFT_01 (SCRAPPED).
That's PATCH's first-draft font. The keepers used his scrapped drafts.
So PATCH wrote the old people's letters? Is weird, bro.

callum.text: KEEPERS' RELAY 1/4. SANCTUARY SIGNAL: WEAK. AWAITING REPLY.
Below it, in tiny letters: FONT: DRAFT_01 (SCRAPPED).
Draft 01. That's PATCH's very first font. I'd know it anywhere.
Ask him. He'll just say he's working on a fix.

lines.text: The screen reads KEEPERS' RELAY 1/4. One bar of signal, flickering.
One bar. Same as my phone at Callum's place.
Strikes, Nolan's cat. Orange, very old, strictly an outside cat.
He was not in the build. I have checked the build. Twice.
He's been outside for like fifteen years. He's fine. He's always fine.

callum.text: Strikes, Nolan's cat. Orange, very old, strictly an outside cat.
STRIKES. Who's the best boy? You are. Don't tell the Patchlings.
Strikes allows exactly one head scratch, then goes back to staring at the horizon.

lines.text: An old lightning rod on a mossy stone, bent like it lost an argument. Runes on the base, all dark.
A grey Tally cable is spliced onto it and runs off to that machine. A tag: PROPERTY OF THE TALLY. WEATHER DIVISION.
A brass lantern hangs off the hook. Inside, where the flame should be, there's an eye. It's barely open.
Nah. Nah. The lamp is looking at me.
It's a Patchling. It's just... dim. Like it ran out of something.

callum.text: An old lightning rod on a mossy stone, bent like it lost an argument. Runes on the base, all dark.
A grey Tally cable is spliced onto it and runs off to that machine.
A brass lantern hangs off the hook. Inside, where the flame should be, there's an eye. It's barely open.
That's a Patchling. A dim one. And that plate's the keepers' writing. I can read that.

lines.text: KEEPERS' RELAY 2/4. STORM-ROD. CALLS THE STORM THE HILLS NEED.
Under it, scratched in later: DO NOT CLAMP.
They clamped it. The Tally spliced the rod into their machine. That's why it never rains here.
So they rain-checked the actual rain.
Bro. They rescheduled weather.
The lamp guy is sad because no storm? ...Same. I like storms. Good for sleeping.
Weather Division. Step away from the Cloud Clamp.
All precipitation on Route 1 has been rain-checked until further notice. Further notice: also rain-checked.
To request weather, fill in Form 12-R. In triplicate. Nobody has ever finished one.
How long is the form?
Nobody knows. Nobody has reached the end.

haydon.text: Weather Division. Step away from the Cloud Clamp.
All precipitation is rain-checked. To request weather, fill in Form 12-R.

dani.text: Weather Division. Step away from the Cloud Clamp.
Hello! We only want a little rain. Small one.
What is triplicate. ...Is three? Three forms? No. I go home.

lines.text: I told him his stamp was crooked. He's going to fix it. It'll take him all day.
Clamp's open. Nolan, you're up.

haydon.text: Told him his stamp was crooked. He's re-stamping everything. Back in a week.

lines.text: The Cloud Clamp. Every time a cloud drifts over, the arm swings up and stamps it: RAIN CHECK. The cloud gives up and leaves.
The storm-rod's cable runs into its side.
I could pull that cable. But someone's guarding it, and I want to know what the rod even does first.
The Clamp stamps another cloud. The storm-rod's cable runs into its side, spliced with tape.
Someone needs to get that cable off and patch the rod back in. That's a Nolan job.
Tally cable off, rod back on the ground line. Should hold.
The Clamp's arm swings up for the next cloud... and stops. Something above it is very, very big.
The Cloud Clamp is jammed, arm up, stamp half-pressed into a rain cloud that didn't care.
A ticket hangs out of the slot: RAIN CHECK... DECLINED.
The storm-rod hums. The runes glow. The lantern on the hook is lit, the eye wide open, watching the sky.
It's waiting for the next storm. It only comes down when it rains.
The storm-rod hums. The runes glow. The hook is empty now: Wardeye went with you.
Rain hits the lantern. The eye inside turns, slowly, and locks onto you.
The lantern lifts off the hook on a curl of smoke!

haydon.text: Rain hits the lantern. The eye inside turns, slowly, and locks onto Haydon.
Don't point that at my phone. I said DON'T—
The lantern lifts off the hook on a curl of smoke!

lines.text: A heavy rock by the storm-rod. Something under it hums, and the grass around it is singed.
A mini fridge. Inside: four energy drinks, a jar of something, and a burger box labelled CALLUM. DO NOT.
Double cheeseburger, extra patty, extra cheese. It's for later.
It has been 'for later' for three days.

dani.text: A mini fridge. Inside: four energy drinks and a burger box labelled CALLUM. DO NOT.
I don't touch. ...I look a little bit.

lines.text: A keyboard and a drum pad on stands, cables everywhere. Nolan's setup, mostly.
Don't touch the levels.
And I picked up a mic and I'm chill.
...Every time.

nolan.text: Your keyboard and drum pad, cables everywhere. The levels are exactly where you left them.
Someone's been on the pad. The kick's in the wrong place.

lines.text: A couch made of crates and every blanket in the sanctuary. Sagging in exactly four places.
Middle seat's mine. That's not up for debate.
The table: wrappers, a burger box, four tangled controllers. Someone has been playing Smash on the old TV.
I'm undefeated on this couch.
No. No, bro. I win two times. Two!
Those were exhibition matches.
A navy beanbag with a Dani-shaped dent in it.
Is the best seat. Don't tell them.
